Supported games

Open one of these ROMs with Open ROM… and ROM Studio switches to that game. You bring the ROM; nothing from the games is in ROM Studio.

The fingerprint (CRC32 / SHA-1) is of the ROM without its 16-byte iNES header, the way No-Intro lists them. A different revision or region of the same game has different code addresses, so it won't open until it gets its own profile.

Super Mario Bros. (World)

Body parts

drawn once, posed everywhere

Right-click or the checkered 0 swatch erases; Pick (or Alt-click) grabs a color. Limbs hang straight down with the joint at the dot; the rig swings them.

Palettes

3 colors each, sky is transparent

Player 2 uses the same drawing as Player 1, recolored. The fire palette is shared by both players.

Stage

click it, then ←→ walk, Space jump, ↓ crouch
MARIO

Game frames

These are the 28 frames the game draws, built from shared 8×8 tiles. A badge counts pixels a frame lost to another frame that uses the same tile. Poses listed first in the rig keep their tiles.

Pose

Offset

Degrees; positive swings a limb forward. Gray names inherit from the pose they copy. × resets to inherited.

rig.yml (parts, skeletons, every pose)

Objects

Goomba

Hover a pixel to see which tile it belongs to.

Palette

Tile

Hover the art to see a tile up close. Click with Tile (T) to pick one and paint it here.

In motion

Painting changes the 8×8 tile itself, so every frame and every object that uses that tile updates together. Hover a pixel to outline its tile everywhere it appears.

Mechanics

These change the game's own numbers and a few of its instructions. Download to get the patched ROM; the values are worked out from your ROM each time.

Sound effects

Jump

Open your ROM to hear and edit the game's sound effects. They're read straight from it.

Each column is one frame (1/60 s). Height is pitch, brightness is volume.

How it works

ROM bytes for this sound

Sound effects are little programs inside the game. You can retune them (pitch, tone, slides, timing, the notes in their tables) but each keeps its basic shape.

Songs

All songs share one small space in the cartridge, about 1.5 KB. To make a song longer, make another one shorter, turn off a song's harmony, or silence a song you don't need.

Overworld

Open your ROM to hear and edit the game's music. The songs are read straight from it.
Overworld arrangement (the order its parts play in)

Rows

Keys: ←→ pick a note, ↑↓ change pitch, 1–8 length, R rest, Enter copy note, Del remove.
